result.title: TALD: Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement for Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
result.summary: Cross-modal knowledge distillation can incur negative transfer when source-modality supervision conflicts with the target modality's discriminative characteristics. We propose TALD, a two-stage framework for Transferability-Aware Logit Disentanglement in class-aligned logit space. Guided by task-dependent self-benefiting and cross-modal exclusivity criteria, a Residual Disentangler decomposes logits from a teacher and an independently trained target-modality reference student into modality-general and modality-specific components. A Sample-Adaptive Modulator regulates decomposition constraints and sample-specific fusion weights. The learned modality-general components are then adaptively fused to supervise the final student. Across five benchmarks spanning vision, audio, and text, TALD achieves the largest mean accuracy gain and highest positive-transfer frequency among the compared methods. Across ten transfer directions with five runs each, TALD improves over training without distillation in 84% of evaluations, compared with at most 70% for the baselines, while offering a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. We plan to release the code.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TALD 两阶段跨模态蒸馏框架，在类别对齐的 logit 空间中将教师与目标模态参考学生的 logit 分解为模态通用与模态特有分量，并用样本自适应调制器调节分解约束与融合权重以缓解负迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按模态拆分表示并做样本自适应融合的思路，可能为 LVR 中区分任务通用信息与视觉特有细节、筛选视觉证据提供可核查线索；但该工作目标是跨模态蒸馏，并非推理期 latent 状态生成。
